extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: A dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernández
extraction.citeAs: Proceedings of the 54th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, pages 1525–1534, Berlin, Germany, August 7-12, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LAMBADA consists of passages composed of a context (on average 4.6 sentences) and a target sentence. The data come from the Book Corpus. Passages were filtered to remove those easy for standard language models. A random sample of the remaining passages were evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service in three steps to ensure the target word is guessable from the whole passage but not from the last sentence alone.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. Random division of novels into training and development+testing partitions. Filtering out passages relatively easy for standard language models using a combination of four language models (a pre-trained RNN, a standard 4-gram model, a RNN, and a feed-forward model); any passage whose target word had probability ≥0.00175 according to any model was excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects evaluated passages via CrowdFlower in three steps: 1) One subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage; 2) If correct, a second subject guessed based on the whole passage; 3) If the second subject was correct, up to 10 subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only (allowed 3 guesses each). If no subject guessed the word in step 3, the passage was added to the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 84–86% items were discarded at step 1, an additional 6–7% at step 2 and another 3–5% at step 3. Only about one in 25 input examples passed all the selection steps. The criteria for inclusion were strict: two consecutive subjects had to exactly match the missing word, and no subject (out of ten) was able to provide it based on local context only.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 positive annotations (guesses based on whole passage) and up to 10 negative annotations (unsuccessful guesses based on target sentence only)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Pre-trained recurrent neural network (RNN), standard 4-gram model, RNN trained on Book Corpus, feed-forward model trained on Book Corpus
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The development set and training corpus are available for download. The test set will be made available at the time of a public competition.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA compared to the POS distribution in the input data. LAMBADA items contain (quoted) direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall (71% vs 61%).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Standard language models are bound to fail on it by design due to the filtering process against simple language models. The strict hit-or-miss approach excludes passages where broad-context subjects provided other plausible or synonymous continuations. The dataset has a low proportion of verbs and adverbs, suggesting it might not effectively test tracking of event-related phenomena compared to co-referential phenomena.
